building: Yue-Kong Pao Hall of Visual and Performing Arts

scorecard.evidence: Purdue GIS FeatureServer layer 0, FID 72, BLDG_ABBR PAO and 552 W Wood Street establish identity. The model bounds are within roughly 1 m of the GIS bbox. Independent polygons from the two actual roof-slab top faces versus the transformed GIS ring have IoU 0.788 and Hausdorff 13.01 m; the slabs are simplified rectangles and do not track the irregular roof outline. Builder source-ring screening reported IoU 0.896 but was not used as a substitute for this check.

The source asset retains campus-coordinate geometry. Fresh read-only master load confirms the relative library link and 363-object asset collection, with no separate placement marker expected for this massing asset. Model/GIS bounding-box side deltas from the recorded transform are under 1.1 m; rotation and exact survey control are not independently proven, and the project geographic conversion is approximate.

The low south public frontage and taller, set-back north performance volume read against the official south-façade photo. The saved asset spans z=-0.065 to 18.87 m. GIS lists six levels and an undocumented Extrution=60 field; roof and penthouse heights remain estimates. Roof slabs are simple flat rectangles, with rooftop equipment represented schematically.

South elevation uses Purdue red brick, repeated tall blue-gray glazed bays, metal mullions/transoms, signage, limestone trim and a west entry canopy consistent with the official PAO exterior photo. The other elevations remain sparse/generic, and exact bay sizes, elevations, and signage letter case/spacing have no dimensional source.

Eleven assigned materials cover brick, Bedford limestone, silver mullions, glazing, roof, and interior surfaces. Brick uses procedural Brick Texture and Bump nodes; all meshes have materials and there are no image dependencies. Finish is coherent but stylized; roof/sides look flat in neutral renders and materials are not photo-mapped.

The model contains lobby/gallery/studio/classroom areas, a dance studio, a black-box stage/acoustic room and 45 studio seats. Purdue program sources support theatres, studios, classrooms, shops, and offices. No architectural floor plans were located; floor distribution and room geometry are representative assumptions, and the larger published theatre programs/capacities are not demonstrated as complete interiors.

Exact candidate freshly reopened in Blender 5.2.3 LTS. Correct scene/collection; 363 mesh objects, 25,382 vertices, 22,839 faces, 11 used materials, no materialless meshes, no image nodes or linked library dependencies. Read-only master check finds the relative asset link and the same 363-object collection. Evidence includes raw Purdue GIS, official PAO image, Esri context image, source register, renders, and explicit height/interior/CRS limits; mesh topology/non-manifold checks and an as-built survey are absent.

independent_geometry_check.source: Purdue ArcGIS BuildingShapesZip4 FeatureServer layer 0, FID 72 / BLDG_ABBR PAO
independent_geometry_check.comparison_transform: Inverse Web Mercator to lon/lat then modular/AGENTS.md local approximation, lon origin -86.9137, lat origin 40.4274
independent_geometry_check.model_geometry: Union of the two actual slab top-face polygons (one low south wing and one high north performance roof slab), extracted from the frozen Blender asset
independent_geometry_check.note: Roof-slab proxy only. It does not represent a surveyed structural wall line. Segmented perimeter meshes and glazing make a direct closed-wall outline ambiguous; this metric exposes the simplified roof-slab coverage and is not claimed as the building footprint score alone.

limitations: GIS polygon is generalized and not surveyed wall line; the local CRS conversion is approximate.
Roof-slab surfaces are simplified rectangles, with independent GIS IoU 0.788 and 13.01 m Hausdorff distance; do not read this proxy as a precise wall outline.
GIS height/unit fields are undocumented; 11.5 m lower roof, 16 m upper roof, and 18.87 m maximum with penthouse are estimates.
Interior is program-informed but schematic; no plan source supports room-by-room layout.
Exterior image evidence is strongest on the south/plaza elevation; side/rear elevations are not verified.
